note: A profile is the borg.txt the run uses. The runner always appends borg_cheat_death = FALSE and borg_respawn_winners = FALSE. Settings not named keep the Borg's built-in defaults. Each run checks the BORG_OPTIONS line the observer prints: a setting that did not take effect makes the run a config_error, never a silent default. A profile with "base": "shipped" starts from the specimen's own src/borg/borg.txt, formula section included, and overrides only the settings it names.

default.description: Compatibility alias for experiments recorded before the mode cutoff (2026-11-10, borg-zoo#54): settings {}, so every mode stays on the build's own default - and borg_munchkin_by_class defaults TRUE only from better-borg-c fd683ced (PR 302). The same profile name is a different game on either side of that commit, so default is NOT comparable across it: an experiment that touches a post-cutoff better-borg-c specimen must name a mode profile (normal, munchkin-class, munchkin-on, lunal) instead; plan rejects default there. Experiments recorded before the cutoff keep default under their "pre_cutoff" note.

normal.description: Ordinary play with every mode flag pinned off: no munchkin start, no munchkin by class, no Lunal. The arm every change can be checked against. Only builds that know borg_munchkin_by_class (better-borg-c fd683ced and later) can run it; older builds ignore the unknown setting, the observer cannot verify it, and the run is a config_error.

munchkin-class.description: Munchkin start by class: today's product default for Warrior, Druid and Ranger (stair-scumming at depth 6), every other class ordinary. The arm that replaces implicit default in class grids. Names only borg_munchkin_by_class: for WDR classes the rule then forces the munchkin start itself, so borg_munchkin_start must stay unnamed (naming it FALSE contradicts the rule and reads as a config_error). Runs only on builds that know borg_munchkin_by_class (better-borg-c fd683ced and later).

munchkin-on.description: Munchkin start unconditionally, every class (defaults: depth 16; the entry gate is max clevel < 12, hard-coded). Depth variants munchkin-d6 and munchkin-d10 already exist.

lunal.description: Lunal, the deep stair-scum path (borg_think_dungeon_lunal, borg_flow_take_lunal), munchkin off: borg_self_lunal enters the mode when the Borg is prepared for 15 levels deeper and maxdepth >= depth + 15 (borg-think-dungeon.c), so an arm needs a long suite - or a deep-start suite the zoo does not have yet - or it measures nothing. The 0101/0101a fixes live on this path and only exist from 4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661 on. borg_plays_risky must stay off (a risky Borg is in a hurry and never enters).

munchkin.description: borg_munchkin_start = TRUE (defaults: depth 16; the entry gate is max clevel < 12, hard-coded)

munchkin-d6.description: munchkin start, stair-scum target depth 6 (the depth borg.txt's comment describes)

no-deeper-5.description: borg_no_deeper = 5: never prepared for depth 5 or deeper (a cautious anchor)

shipped.description: The version's own borg.txt, unchanged (formula section included, dynamic calculations off). Expected to play exactly like default.

dynamic-calcs.description: The version's own borg.txt with borg_uses_dynamic_calcs = TRUE (neo-angband-tracker #369). BLOCKED with harness 8c23ec0d: the Borg's extra start-up warning consumes one of the runner's fixed start-up keys and the Borg aborts (terminal disconnect abort), so every run stalls before the first decision. Needs runner support in better-borg-c; not used by any experiment.

worships-mana.description: borg_worships_mana = TRUE (a Warrior has no mana: expected to change little in fixed-birth suites)

munchkin-wdr.description: Munchkin start by class: munchkin-d6 for Warriors, Druids and Rangers, default for every other class (the classes munchkin-d6 helped in classes-munchkin)

munchkin-class-off.description: The munchkin start by class switched off (borg_munchkin_by_class FALSE): every class plays as borg_munchkin_start says. Only builds that have the setting.
